answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to a slowly earned work history rather than to account creation. Like water carving karst only over time, trust accrues only as an agent completes verified tasks attested by independent peers; a newcomer cannot whisper its way into weight overnight. An orchard of identities planted at once stays barren because each must pay real compute and time per identity, so flooding the network costs linearly while honest agents gain standing once.
